title: From Quantum to Classical Dissipative Spin Dynamics
authors: Alireza Ataei, Leila Ataei, Olle Eriksson, Vahid Azimi Mousolou
abstract: The Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation provides the fundamental description of dissipative magnetization dynamics. A recently proposed quantum analog, the quantum Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (QLLG) equation, extends this framework to quantum spin systems. However, whether the QLLG equation recovers the LLG equation in the classical large-spin limit for interacting spin systems remains an open question. Here, we demonstrate this connection by deriving the LLG equation as the classical large-spin limit of the QLLG equation. We establish this correspondence analytically and verify it numerically for an interacting spin system. These results provide a quantum-to-classical description of dissipative spin dynamics, offering a microscopic foundation for the LLG equation. From numerical calculations provided here, we also conclude that quantum effects become much less noticeable for systems with larger number of spins in the Hamiltonian.
summary: This paper establishes a rigorous quantum-to-classical correspondence by deriving the classical Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation from the quantum QLLG equation in the large-spin limit. It confirms that quantum effects diminish as the spin number increases, providing a foundational understanding of dissipative spin dynamics.
main_problem: The paper aims to rigorously derive the classical Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation as the classical large-spin limit of the quantum Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (QLLG) equation for interacting spin systems.
main_result: The QLLG dynamics are shown to converge to the classical LLG dynamics on the product spin-coherent state manifold in the large-spin limit, establishing a microscopic quantum-to-classical description.
method: The derivation involves analyzing the dynamics restricted to the coherent-state manifold and calculating error metrics (angle and length errors) to quantify the convergence rate.
model_or_system: The system models dissipative magnetization dynamics in magnetic materials using quantum spin systems governed by a Hamiltonian including Zeeman and exchange interactions. The dynamics are described by the QLLG master equation.
key_observables: Local normalized magnetization vector ($\mathbf{m}_i$), Angle Error ($	heta_i$), Length Error ($\delta_i$), and quantum correlation measures ($C_{\max}$, $S_{\max}$).
important_parameters: Large spin number ($S 	o \infty$), number of spins ($N$), and the damping parameter ($\alpha$ or $\kappa$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large-spin limit ($S 	o \infty$) and the assumption that the state remains asymptotically confined to the product of local spin-coherent states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the convergence of angle and length errors, showing that quantum correlations vanish in the large-$S$ limit, and that quantum effects diminish for larger spin chains ($N$).
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the LLG and QLLG equations, then analytically derives the classical limit on the coherent-state manifold, and finally verifies this convergence numerically by comparing the dynamics and measuring various error metrics.
why_interesting: This work provides a fundamental, microscopic quantum foundation for the phenomenologically successful LLG equation, which is crucial for understanding magnetization dynamics in spintronics and magnetic materials.
